title: Inherited abstract methods and concrete subclasses
answer: When a class inherits an abstract method and does not implement it, that subclass must also be declared abstract. The obligation travels down the inheritance chain until some concrete subclass supplies a compatible implementation. This differs from merely declaring an abstract method in the current class, but both rules ensure directly instantiable classes are behaviorally complete.
